problems.title: A radical restricts the candidate roots
problems.question: Solve √x·(x³+64)=0.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Domain x≥0. A zero product requires√x=0 or x³+64=0.
steps: The candidates are0 and−4. Only0 belongs to the domain.

problems.title: Roots symmetric about a specified point
problems.question: For which a are the roots of (a+3)x²−2x−a−3=0 symmetric about x=2?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The root midpoint is $-B/(2A)=1/(a+3)$.
steps: Set1/(a+3)=2 to obtain a=−5/2. The leading coefficient is1/2,so the equation remains quadratic and its discriminant is positive.

problems.title: Tangent of the smaller angle in a right triangle
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuse2√5 and one leg4. Find tangent of its smaller angle.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The other leg is $\sqrt{(2\sqrt5)^2-4^2}=2$.
steps: The smaller angle is opposite the shorter leg2,so its tangent is2/4=1/2.

problems.title: An equation true for every input
problems.question: If2ax−3b=5x−1 has infinitely many roots,find a+b.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Both coefficients must match:2a=5,3b=1.

problems.title: Check every zero of a system determinant
problems.question: Find a for which (3−a)x+2ay=−11,(3a−1)x−ay=10/3 has no solution.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The determinant is $-a(1+5a)$. Only a=0 or−1/5 can fail uniqueness.
steps: At a=0,the equations give x=−11/3 and x=−10/3,so they conflict.
At a=−1/5,the second left side is−1/2 of the first,but10/3 is not(−1/2)(−11)=11/2,so they also conflict.
Every other a has nonzero determinant and exactly one solution.
problems.note: The printed choices offer−1/5 but omit0. Both are valid no-solution parameters.

problems.title: Height of a trapezoid from a three-four-five triangle
problems.question: A trapezoid has legs3,4 and bases7.5,12.5. Find height.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The base difference is5. Together with the two legs,it forms a triangle of sides3,4,5.
steps: That triangle is right,with area3·4/2=6. Its altitude to the side5 equals the trapezoid height.
Thus5h/2=6,giving h=12/5=2.4.

problems.title: A nontrivial interval contains infinitely many rationals
problems.question: For which a does x≤3,x≥a have exactly one rational solution?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The solution set is [a,3] if a≤3,and empty otherwise.
steps: If a<3,the interval has positive length and contains infinitely many rationals. If a>3,it has none.
Only a=3 gives the singleton{3},with exactly one rational member.

problems.title: Distance from the centre to a split chord
problems.question: A diameter crosses a chord at angleα and splits it into15 and7. If tanα=2,find centre-to-chord distance.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The chord midpoint H is11 from either endpoint,so its distance from the crossing point M is4. OH is perpendicular to the chord.
steps: In right triangle OMH,the angle atM has tangent OH/MH=2. Therefore OH=4·2=8.

problems.title: Rhombus diagonals bisect angles
problems.question: A rhombus’s diagonals are in ratio1:√3. Find its obtuse angle.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Half-diagonals and a side make a right triangle with legs in ratio1:√3.
steps: Its acute angles are30° and60°. A diagonal bisects the rhombus vertex angle,so the rhombus angles are60° and120°.

problems.title: Simplify the reciprocal of a defined operation
problems.question: For a⊗b=a/(a−b),with a,b>0,which listed assertion is always true?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: $1/(a\otimes b)=(a-b)/a=1-b/a<1$.
steps: Because b/a>0,the reciprocal is always less than1. This works whether a−b is positive or negative.
problems.note: The operation is undefined at a=b. The assertion applies where the displayed operation is defined.

problems.title: Check parity of each statement
problems.question: k is even and p odd. Which assertion is false: p−k−1 odd;p+k+1 even;pk+p odd;p²+k²+1 even?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: An odd number minus an even number minus1 is even.
steps: Thus p−k−1 is even,so the first assertion is false.
The others are true:odd+even+1 is even;pk+p=even+odd is odd;odd²+even²+1 is even.

problems.title: Divide numerator and denominator by cosine
problems.question: Evaluate(7sinα−5cosα)/(4sinα+3cosα),given tanα=1/2.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The ratio is $(7\tan\alpha-5)/(4\tan\alpha+3)$.

problems.title: Add strict bounds
problems.question: Given2<a<5,−3<b<−1,find the range of3a−2b.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
steps: Adding gives8<3a−2b<21.

problems.title: Square a reciprocal sum
problems.question: If x+1/x=45,find x²+1/x².
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
steps: Subtract2 from45²=2025. The required value is2023.

problems.title: Time for the remaining distance after doubling speed
problems.question: A traveller covers3/8 of a route in6h. How long for the remaining part at twice the speed?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Time is proportional to distance and inversely proportional to speed.
steps: The remaining distance is5/8,which is5/3 of the initial distance. At twice speed,the time is6·(5/3)/2=5h.

problems.title: Distances from a circumcentre to perpendicular legs
problems.question: A right triangle is inscribed in a radius-√3 circle. One leg is√3 times closer to the centre than the other. Find the longer leg.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Put the right-angle vertex at the origin and legs on the axes. The circumcentre is the hypotenuse midpoint,so distances to the legs are half the opposite leg lengths.
steps: The leg lengths therefore have ratio1:√3. Write them t and√3t.
The hypotenuse is2√3,so t²+3t²=12 and t=√3. The longer leg is3.

problems.title: Parallel lines have the same slope
problems.question: Line a is3x−5y+7=0. A parallel line crosses Oy at−3. Find its equation.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The first line has slope3/5=0.6.
steps: Keep this slope and use intercept−3: y=0.6x−3.

problems.title: A half-line positivity set forces a linear polynomial
problems.question: The solutions of ax²+bx+c>0 are exactly(−5,∞). Find(a+c)/b.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: A genuine quadratic has the same end behaviour at both infinities,so cannot be positive on exactly one half-line. Thus a=0.
steps: The linear inequality bx+c>0 has this solution set only if b>0 and c=5b.
Hence(a+c)/b=5.

problems.title: When an absolute value equals its input
problems.question: Solve|x²−2x|=x²−2x.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: $|u|=u$ exactly when u≥0.
steps: Solve x(x−2)≥0. The product is nonnegative for x≤0 or x≥2,including both zeros.

problems.title: A quadratic strictly positive everywhere
problems.question: Find all a for which ax²+x+a>0 for every real x.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Require a>0 and discriminant1−4a²<0.
steps: A nonpositive leading coefficient cannot give positivity everywhere. For a>0,the discriminant condition gives a>1/2.
Equality a=1/2 is excluded because the polynomial then has a zero.

problems.title: Place two roots on opposite sides of an interval
problems.question: For which a does x²−(a−2)x−a=0 have one root below1 and the other above2?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: For an upward quadratic,this is equivalent to P(1)<0 and P(2)<0.
steps: The stronger condition a>8/3 ensures both1 and2 lie strictly between two distinct real roots.

problems.title: Roots after replacing the input by its absolute value
problems.question: f(x)=0 has four positive roots,two negative roots,and zero. How many roots has f(|x|)=0?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Each positive root r gives x=±r;zero gives x=0;negative roots cannot be |x|.
steps: Thus the count is2·4+1=9.

problems.title: Acute angle between a line and an axis
problems.question: Find the sine of the acute angle between y=−x+3 and Ox.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The absolute slope is1,so the acute angle is45°.
steps: Its sine is√2/2. The negative slope does not make the acute angle negative.

problems.title: Root product cannot be negative
problems.question: For which real a does x²−(a²+5)x+3a²+6=0 have two roots with negative product?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: By Vieta,the root product is3a²+6>0 for every real a.
steps: It can never be negative,so no parameter satisfies the request.

problems.title: An angle bisector locates an equidistant centre
problems.question: A triangle has sides39,65,80. A circle touches the two smaller sides and has centre on the largest side. Find the difference of the two pieces of that side.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The centre is on the internal angle bisector,so the side pieces are in ratio39:65=3:5.
steps: Their sum is80,so they are30 and50. Their difference is20.

problems.title: Square an absolute-value inequality safely
problems.question: Solve|2x−1|<|x|.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Both sides are nonnegative,so square: $(2x-1)^2<x^2$.
steps: Simplification gives3x²−4x+1<0,or(3x−1)(x−1)<0. Thus1/3<x<1.

problems.title: Classify a triangle by its longest side
problems.question: Classify the triangle with sides7,8,11.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Triangle existence:7+8>11. Compare11² with7²+8².
steps: 121>49+64=113,so the angle opposite11 is obtuse by the cosine rule.

problems.title: Four intersections with an absolute-value parabola
problems.question: For which a do y=|x²−2x−8| and y=a have four intersection points?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: $x^2-2x-8=(x-1)^2-9$. Split into the equations P(x)=a and P(x)=−a.
steps: For a>0,the first equation has two roots because(x−1)²=9+a. The second has two distinct roots exactly when9−a>0.
At a=0,the two equations coincide. At a=9,one pair merges. Thus four distinct points require0<a<9.

problems.title: A rational equation with excluded denominators
problems.question: Solve9/(x²−4)=3/(x²−4)−2.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Domain x≠±2. Multiply by x²−4 after combining fractions.
steps: 6/(x²−4)=−2 gives x²−4=−3,so x²=1. Both x=−1 and1 are valid.

problems.title: Two layers of absolute value
problems.question: How many roots has||x−6|−6|=4?
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Let u=|x−6|≥0. Then|u−6|=4 gives u=10 or2.
steps: For u=10,the roots are−4,16. For u=2,the roots are4,8. All four are distinct.

problems.title: Distance between two motions on rays
problems.question: Two objects move from one point along rays120° apart at4 and5km/h. Find their separation after2h.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Cosine rule: $d^2=8^2+10^2-2\cdot8\cdot10\cos120^\circ$.
steps: Since cos120°=−1/2,the result is64+100+80=244. Thus d=2√61km.

problems.title: An isosceles triangle hidden in a tangential trapezoid
problems.question: A circle is inscribed in trapezoid ABCD. CK is perpendicular to baseAD,O is the circle centre,M midpoint of legCD. If angleOKM=55°,find OMK.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Let circle radius r and angleCDA=θ. Use D=(0,0),C=(2r cotθ,2r). Then K=(2r cotθ,0),M=(r cotθ,r),O=(r cot(θ/2),r).
steps: OM=r[cot(θ/2)−cotθ]=r cscθ. Also MK=√[(r cotθ)²+r²]=r cscθ.
Thus OM=MK,so the base angles atO andK are equal,each55°. The angle atM is180°−110°=70°.

problems.title: Weighted concentration of a mixture
problems.question: Mix2L of30% alcohol with6L of20% alcohol. Find final concentration.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Alcohol volume=2·0.30+6·0.20=1.8L;total volume8L.
steps: The fraction is1.8/8=0.225,or22.5%.

problems.title: A trapezoid with both an incircle and circumcircle
problems.question: A bicentric trapezoid has base sum equal to circumcircle diameter and diagonal20. Find inradius.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: A cyclic trapezoid is isosceles. Tangency gives equal leg l=(a+b)/2;the diameter condition gives R=l.
steps: For the triangle formed by a base,a leg and a diagonal d,the circumradius formula gives R=ld/(2h). Since R=l,we obtain d=2h.
Thus h=10. The incircle touches both parallel bases,so its diameter is h and its radius is5.

problems.title: A midpoint quadrilateral in a right triangle
problems.question: A right triangle has hypotenuseAB=30. Medians AN,BM meet atO;K,P are midpoints of AO,BO. Find perimeter KPNM.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Put C=(0,0),A=(u,0),B=(0,v),withu²+v²=900. Then O=(u/3,v/3).
steps: Distances give KP=MN=√(u²+v²)/2=15 and PN=MK=√(u²+v²)/6=5.
The perimeter is15+5+15+5=40.

problems.title: Root separation of a quadratic
problems.question: The roots of2x²−2x+k=0 differ by2. Find k.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Root sum=1. Roots with midpoint1/2 and separation2 are−1/2 and3/2.
steps: Their product is−3/4. By Vieta,this equals k/2,so k=−3/2.

problems.title: Power of a point on a secant
problems.question: A point is√7 from a circle centre. A secant’s internal part equals radiusR and is half its external part. Find R.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: External segment=2R,whole secant=3R;power=$7-R^2=(2R)(3R)$.
steps: Thus7=7R². A positive radius givesR=1.

problems.title: A tangent and secant determine a radius ratio
problems.question: A circle touches one side of angleA atB and intersects the other atD,C,with AC=3AD. If cosA=√3/4,find R/BD.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Let AD=t,AC=3t. Tangent power gives AB=√3t. Choose A=(0,0),D=(t,0),C=(3t,0).
steps: Then B=(3t/4,√39t/4). A circle throughD,C has centreO=(2t,z). The tangent condition OB⊥AB gives O·B=|B|²=3t².
Solving gives z=6t/√39,so R²=t²+z²=25t²/13.
The cosine rule in triangleABD gives BD²=3t²+t²−2√3t²·√3/4=5t²/2.

problems.title: Minimise a weighted square sum
problems.question: Distinct positive a,b satisfy a²−2022a=b²−2022b. Minimise a²+2b².
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: Factoring gives$(a-b)(a+b-2022)=0$;since a≠b,we have a+b=2022.
steps: Seta=2022−b. Completing the square gives a²+2b²=3(b−674)²+2725656.
The minimum occurs atb=674,a=1348,both positive and distinct.

problems.title: Largest rectangle inscribed against a triangle base
problems.question: A triangle has basea and heighth. An inscribed rectangle has two vertices on that base. Find maximum rectangle area.
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: At heighty,the triangle width is a(1−y/h),so rectangle area A(y)=ay(1−y/h).
steps: Complete the square:A(y)=ah/4−(a/h)(y−h/2)².
The maximum isah/4,attained at height h/2 and width a/2.

problems.title: Constrain the maximum of a parameter parabola
problems.question: For f(x)=1+ax−x² on[1,2],find all a for which its maximum lies in(3,10).
problems.idea: Use the structure of the equation or figure,and verify the full set of possibilities.
formulas: The vertex isx=a/2. Maximum M(a)=a for a≤2;1+a²/4 for2≤a≤4;2a−3 for a≥4.
steps: For a≤2,the maximum cannot exceed3. In the middle range,3<1+a²/4<10 givesa>2√2,with a≤4.
For a≥4,the condition3<2a−3<10 gives4≤a<13/2.
Combining the two valid pieces gives2√2<a<13/2.
